funding_share_basis: The purse is a USD 250,000 cash award plus a gold medal, endowed in full by the New York-based G. Unger Vetlesen Foundation, a private foundation created by shipping magnate Georg Unger Vetlesen shortly before his death in 1955; Lamont-Doherty (Columbia University) administers selection and the jury but is not identified as a purse contributor, so the foundation supplies 100% (>50%) in both the origin and current state. No other funder was found.
money_note: Current prize is USD 250,000 plus a gold medal and travel to the Vetlesen Lecture; endowed by the G. Unger Vetlesen Foundation since the prize's establishment in 1959.
status_note: Awarded on average once every two to three years; most recent laureate is David Kohlstedt (2023), and as of August 2026 the official page says only that the next call for nominations is pending.
evidence_quote: Endowed by the New York-based G. Unger Vetlesen Foundation and administered by the Columbia Climate School's Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, the award is bestowed 'for scientific achievement resulting in a clearer understanding of the Earth...'
judgment_reason: Wikipedia describes the prize as awarded 'jointly' by Lamont-Doherty and the G. Unger Vetlesen Foundation, so a coder could set awarding_org_type to Philanthropy. I coded University because the official prize page states the prize 'is administered by Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory' and that selection is made by a five-member jury appointed by the president of Columbia University; the foundation supplies the money and co-hosts the banquet.
